subject: AcmeCloud: integration exemptions, entitlement mapping, and rollout tradeoffs
messages:
From: Sophie Ramos <sophie@acmecloud.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.example>
Cc: platform@acmecloud.com
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial: integration checklist and potential marketplace exemption

Hi Mateo —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our platform team pulled together a short list of questions so we can map Redwood into AcmeCloud Marketplace and avoid a staging entitlement roadblock that blocked a previous partner. Key asks:

- Entitlement mapping: we need a way to reconcile marketplace SKUs to Redwood account-level entitlements (per-customer seat vs token quotas).
- SSO & audit: SAML attributes we must exchange and retention/audit log evidence for SOC2 review.
- Billing & refunds: invoice reconciliation cadence and whether Redwood supports marketplace-managed billing with pass-through refunds.
- Sandbox exemption: can Redwood accept a temporary "sandbox" entitlement for partners during onboarding that is exempt from production quotas?

I attached our integration requirements spreadsheet (acme-integration-requirements.xlsx). Can you loop in the right people on your side and let us know what falls under product vs legal vs infra?

Appreciate it —
Sophie Ramos
Head of Platform Partnerships
AcmeCloud

Cc'ing Sophie so they can see our internal thread. Lauren — can you outline product constraints and ETA on a mapping API? Stephanie — flag any infra data-retention privacy blockers. Aditya — I may need a short commercial concession to enable a marketplace exemption window.

Thanks, Mateo. Quick product notes after review of their spreadsheet:

- Entitlement mapping: we currently expose per-customer quota and plan tier via the /v1/entitlements endpoint, but it only supports plan-level SKU mapping, not third-party marketplace SKU reconciliation. Building a mapping table that correlates marketplace SKU -> internal plan_id is a medium-effort task (2 sprints).

- Sandbox exemption: we can add a temporary flag on account objects (sandbox_exempt_until) that bypasses quota enforcement for onboarding. This is low-risk but needs an audit trail (we'll log the exemption event).

- SSO/audit: we have SAML attribute statements and can provide exported logs (syslog or GCS). Retention defaults are 90 days; extending beyond that for partners needs Legal approval.

Technical ETA estimates:
- Mapping table prototype: 10 business days (API + admin UI to configure mappings).
- Sandbox exemption + audit logging: 3 business days for backend + ops checklist.

I'll attach the entitlement API spec draft for internal review.

Lauren Bishop
Product Manager, Marketplace Integrations
Redwood Inference

Good notes. From sales/procurement perspective:

- We should allow a sandbox_exempt window of 30 days for onboarding, tied to a signed mutual action plan (MAP). After 30 days we either flip to marketplace entitlements or require a commercial uplift.
- Commercial concession: I can authorize a marketplace onboarding credit up to $10k in consumed tokens for qualified partners; anything above requires director approval.
- Procurement: AcmeCloud will need a PO flow or DocuSign. If they want marketplace-managed billing with pass-through refunds, we must mirror that in the contract addendum.

I'll prepare a short MAP and send DocuSign link to Sophie after we confirm the technical approach. Putting deal id ACME-2027-019 on my calendar.

Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Initial: integration checklist and potential marketplace exemption

Looping infra concerns — short summary and recommended fallback:

- Audit artifacts: we can provide SAML assertions and event logs. For SOC2 evidence, we can generate a filtered export (JSON) for specific customers; we will need explicit consent / legal note if retention > 90 days.
- Quota bypass: implementing sandbox_exempt is trivial; we must ensure the KV cache and batching layers respect the bypass for low-latency requests. QA pass required to validate load under sandbox mode.
- Fallback plan: If mapping table is not ready in 10 days, propose an interim manual mapping process: Acme sends SKU->plan mapping CSV, we ingest to a managed mapping service and reconcile nightly. This avoids blocking their staging run.

Actionable next steps (I suggest we confirm in 48 hours):
1) Product agrees to start prototype mapping API (Lauren) — ETA 10 business days.
2) Infra builds sandbox_exempt flag + audit log hook (Stephanie) — ETA 3 business days.
3) Sales prepares MAP and DocuSign (Aditya) — target to sign within 72 hours to enable sandbox window.

I attached a draft mutual action plan (ACME_Redwood_Mutual_Action_Plan_v1.pdf) for their review. Once signed we can flip the exemption on from our admin console.

Thanks —
Stephanie Nguyen
Sr. Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
